decisions.executionNote: Begin a small elbow-up right-arm approach; inspect wrist direction before approaching the set square. Left arm remains at origin.
Raise and advance the right wrist while rotating its fingers toward the tabletop, maintaining the same elbow branch.
Continue turning the right gripper forward above the right end of the set square, staying clear of the cubes.
Shift toward a right-side grip point while continuing the downward wrist rotation, with clearance above the set square.
Finish most of the downward rotation above the ruler's right-hand section; retain height until the jaw alignment is correct.
RGB indicates the finger axis was rotated past vertical. Correct the pitch while keeping the tool clear of the table.
Set the finger approach vertically downward, then begin yawing the open jaws across the narrow width of the set square.
Yaw the downward-facing open gripper to straddle the set square near its right end; approach remains above the surface.
Complete the jaw yaw alignment and lower gradually toward the set square without contacting any block.
Fine-align over the right section and descend slowly so the open fingertips straddle the ruler at tabletop height.
Close on the set square at surface height and make a tiny planar test motion; verify retention from the ruler movement, not the gripper command.
The ruler is between the jaws. Level its long edge in the table plane while keeping all cubes untouched and unlifted.
Correct the remaining ruler skew and begin a slow, level push toward the staggered cubes. Keep the held ruler at surface height.
Advance the nearly horizontal straightedge evenly toward the nearest cube, using only tabletop sliding motion.
Make a final small straightedge yaw correction while advancing into gentle contact with the nearest cube.
The nearest two cubes are meeting the straightedge. Continue the same slow planar push to bring the third into the aligned row.
All three are at the straightedge; make a short, slow finishing push to square their faces and settle them into one row without lifting.
The three cubes now appear straight and parallel. Withdraw the straightedge a short distance along the table before releasing it and resetting the arm.
Release the straightedge onto the tabletop, then lift only the empty gripper. The aligned cubes remain undisturbed.
Retract the empty right hand clear of the row while unwinding its yaw. Correct the tiny left-arm drift back toward its starting pose.
Continue retracting through the right workspace with the empty gripper, progressively restoring its original yaw.
Finish unwinding the right wrist yaw while moving away from the set square; keep the elbow-up configuration continuous.
Restore the right arm's starting pitch and position gradually along the reverse approach path, leaving the aligned row untouched.
Continue the gradual right-arm reset along the same configuration, with open fingers and no further contact with the objects.
Slow the final reset near the home configuration, keeping joint changes small and preserving the completed row.
